heading: Measuring effective parameters can turn double descent into a U-shaped curve
definition: measured against an appropriate effective number of parameters, the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
summary: The claim is contested and depends on the complexity measure. Test-time effective parameters recover U-shaped curves for trees, boosting and random Fourier features on MNIST, while another measure retains second descent in random Fourier features and random forests.

suggested_status.by_scale: Contested in the classical-model and neural-network settings described, whose parameter sizes are unspecified. No size-specific level can be assigned for toy, <1B, 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B from versions.V7.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: Direct support remains: MNIST 0-vs-all regression trees, gradient boosting and RFF yield U-folding against test-time effective parameters (arXiv:2310.18988#R10, arXiv:2310.18988#R11, arXiv:2310.18988#R12). The coefficient-norm U-curve in arXiv:2403.08160#r5 does not measure an effective parameter count and is not a test of exact V7. Norm-based regime-dependent branches qualify the ordinary-U wording (arXiv:2502.01585#R7, arXiv:2502.01585#R9); persistence under that study's alternative measures is limits_scope, not challenges. C is retained for the checker-confirmed persistence of second descent under GAC in MNIST RFF and random forests (arXiv:2605.21167#r2, arXiv:2605.21167#r5). GAC disappearance for the CIFAR neural network and gradient boosting establishes only partial V7 (arXiv:2605.21167#r9, arXiv:2605.21167#r11); the MNIST neural-network result also has an initialization confound (arXiv:2605.21167#r7). These comparisons do not establish a failed replication using the same effective-parameter definition. counts: versions.V7.verdicts contains pre-correction labels; versions.V7.studies_by_size supplies only 'not stated'.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched comparison applying a stated effective-parameter definition across the same model sweeps could separate measure dependence from replication failure. Direct deep-network error-versus-effective-parameter plots, a criterion for choosing the measure independently of the observed curve, and tests along epoch and sample axes would clarify the claim's scope.

source.title: Deep double descent: where bigger models and more data hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

original_result.result: No original paper is identified for this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Overparameterized least-squares risk became U-shaped when plotted against predictive degrees of freedom, a measure of flexibility.
CIFAR-10 VAE curves showed double descent only after combining parameter axes.
Random-feature test error tracked squared weight norms as estimated VC-dimension fell beyond the threshold.
MNIST regression curves became convex U-shapes against test-time effective parameters.
Random-feature ridge regression error became U-shaped when plotted against the normalized sum of squared coefficients.
Deep-network test-time effective parameters decreased after the threshold, indirectly suggesting U-shaped curves.
Regression models with excess parameters matched simpler models in flexibility measured on random inputs.
Separating predictor flexibility and model count resolved genomic prediction’s double descent into U-shaped and L-shaped curves.
A complexity measure removed double descent in models with changing features, without establishing a standard U-shape.
Effective dimensionality removed second descent but yielded a near-linear relation among interpolating linear models.
Least-squares regression needed separate U-shaped curves when parameters were fewer versus more numerous than training examples.
Random-forest curves sloped downward when plotted against average flexibility per tree.
Varying variational autoencoder parameters sometimes yielded L-shaped curves or curves moving one way, rather than U-shapes.
Learning capacity removed second descent, but test loss rose or stayed flat.
Magnitude-based capacity removed second descent but yielded separate U-shaped curves and curves moving in one direction.
A measure was argued to preserve double descent by changing in one direction as dimension varied.
Double descent persisted against several complexity measures based on flexibility (degrees of freedom) or vector lengths.
A complexity measure preserved second descent in random Fourier features and random forests with fixed features.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether the same effective-parameter reparameterization turns epoch-wise or sample-wise double descent into an ordinary U.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.main_rows_by_operation contains scaling and measurement only. arXiv:2106.15682#r3 (Section 4.3) reparameterizes a subset-size sweep at fixed n = 20 and d = 100; no epoch-wise or sample-wise double-descent reparameterization is reported. The paper does not explicitly list these axes as untested.

untested.what: Direct test-error-versus-test-time-effective-parameter U-curves for deep neural networks.
untested.basis: arXiv:2310.18988 lists deep networks as untested; arXiv:2411.00247#R6 and #R7 track effective parameters but its untested-parts line states that test error is not directly plotted against them. GAC and path-norm tests use different measures. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.measurement does not identify a direct deep-network p_test plot.

untested.what: Size-resolved replication in large language models and across the catalog's parameter-size buckets.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size contains only 'not stated'; versions.V7.studies_by_family contains only 'other or not stated'. The pack supplies no size-resolved transformer or language-model test. Missing size metadata prevents treating this as proof that every tested model lies below a particular scale.

wording_issues.issue: The outcome depends on the chosen complexity measure. Test-time effective parameters yield U-folding in the MNIST 0-vs-all non-neural experiments, whereas GAC preserves second descent for MNIST RFF and random forests, and MDL-COMP is argued to preserve it in OLS. These records do not specify a common selection criterion for 'appropriate'.

Related findings do not test this exact wording. Random feature ridge regression changes from double descent versus feature count to a U-shaped curve versus normalized squared coefficient norm, which is not an effective parameter count. The random-feature SVM/LS study supplies a VC-dimension bound and norm-based explanation, without establishing an effective-count replot. The CIFAR-10 VAE and tree/boosting studies separate raw capacity axes without computing effective parameter counts. Their V7 result is cannot_determine, rather than support or a measured scope limit.

Subset least-squares prediction error against log predictive degrees of freedom yields a U within each separately treated fitting procedure, but two similar U-curves across the combined regimes: partial for V7 overall. Random-feature norm plots have distinct branches described as φ-shaped. For one- and two-layer fully connected MNIST networks with 10–100 hidden neurons, loss-versus-learning-capacity slopes are positive at N = 200, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000 and 10,000 (p < 0.005); at N = 50,000 the slope is not significantly nonzero. These regressions exclude LeNet and do not establish an ordinary U. Disappearance of second descent alone does not establish the specified shape.

Some evidence stops short of directly showing the transformation. Single-hidden-layer neural-network width sweeps on CIFAR-10 cat-versus-dog and MNIST-1D track declining test-time effective parameters without an error-versus-effective-parameter plot. Under GAC, double descent disappears for CIFAR-10 neural networks and gradient boosting, without an explicitly established ordinary U: partial for V7, with limits_scope verdicts. The MNIST neural-network GAC result is likewise partial and limits_scope; initialization changes from trained weights below the transition to random initialization above it, confounding that comparison.

method_sensitivity.what: MNIST 0-vs-all RFF and regression-tree results fold into U-shapes under test-time effective parameters: V7 is observed, while V4's double-descent shape is absent after reparameterization. MNIST RFF and random forests retain second descent under GAC. These comparisons use different complexity definitions rather than matched replications of the same reparameterization.

Second-layer coefficient norm in random-feature models and path norm in neural networks remove second descent but retain distinct underparameterized and overparameterized branches. The study reports persistence under first-layer Frobenius norm in random-feature models, Frobenius norm and spectral complexity in two-layer networks, and df1/df2 in linear ridge regression. These findings establish measure dependence, warranting limits_scope rather than challenges for V7. In subset least squares, predictive-degrees-of-freedom plots contain two similar U-shaped curves when the fitting regimes are considered together; V7 is observed within each separately treated procedure and partial across both.

method_sensitivity.factor: Feature learning and initialization under GAC
method_sensitivity.what: GAC retains second descent for constant-feature MNIST RFF and random forests. Double descent disappears under GAC for the CIFAR neural network and gradient boosting, without explicitly establishing an ordinary U-shaped curve; these are partial V7 results warranting limits_scope. The MNIST neural-network result likewise establishes disappearance only and changes initialization across regimes, from trained-weight initialization below the transition to random initialization above it. The CIFAR neural-network comparison uses the same random initialization scheme across sizes.

One- and two-layer fully connected networks with 10–100 hidden neurons on MNIST show positive loss-versus-learning-capacity regression slopes, p < 0.005, at N = 200, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000 and 10,000. At N = 50,000, the slope is not significantly nonzero. LeNet is not included in these regressions.

In the CIFAR-10 neural-network width sweep, training effective parameters increase while test-time effective parameters fall beyond the threshold. The claimed fold-back specifically uses the test-time measure.
